value.title: DRDGOLD production up 10%, operating profit up 42%, free cash inflow R725m
value.snippet: Gold tailings mining company DRDGOLD has reported a strong start to its 2027 financial year (FY2027), with higher gold production, improved yields and stronger operating profit for the quarter ended September 30. Gold production increased despite a 5% reduction in tonnage throughput to 6.2-million tonnes. Revenue increased by 31%, supported by a 14% increase in gold sold and a 14% improvement in the average rand gold price received.

value.title: Upstream energy investor EnCap secures $3.5bn commitments for EnCap Minerals continuation vehicle

value.title: China's Australian coal imports surge to six-year high
value.snippet: China's coal imports from Australia surged in September to their highest level since April 2020, before Beijing's unofficial ban on Australian coal imports disrupted trade, customs data showed on Tuesday. Shipments from Australia rose 56% from a year earlier to 9.81-million metric tons, customs data showed, the highest since April 2020, before a political rift disrupted coal purchases for much of 2021 and 2022.

value.title: High-purity nickel producer Westwin secures extended offtake with Traxys worth $3.9bn
value.snippet: US-based nickel refiner Westwin Elements has announced an amended agreement with metals trader Traxys whereby Westwin may extend its existing feedstock and nickel offtake arrangements with Traxys for a total term of up to 22 years. The amended and restated agreements give Westwin a long-term pathway to secure feedstock and offtake as it expands its US production, reducing commercial risk while strengthening the domestic nickel supply chain.

value.title: Hormuz could be 'redundant' in five years, replaced by new routes, HSBC CEO says

The conflict has highlighted the world's heavy reliance on the strategic waterway, through which a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade previously passed.

value.title: Kumba Iron Ore’s third-quarter sales up 3%, average price 9% above benchmark
value.snippet: As planned, the iron-ore production of Kumba Iron Ore in the three months to September 30 was lower, largely owing to the ultrahigh-dense-media-separation (UHDMS) project tie-in at Sishen, but third-quarter sales were supported by the drawdown of finished stock lifting sales to a 3%-higher ten-million tons. Market conditions softened through the quarter as weaker Chinese steel production, compressed mill margins and strong seaborne supply weighed on prices, but despite these headwinds, Kumba continued to realise a premium to benchmark prices, underpinned by the quality of its lump iron-ore products and its diversified customer base.

value.title: Marc Cameron to join Weir as minerals division president
value.snippet: Marc Cameron will join Weir as president of the minerals division on October 26 and become a member of the group executive. In a media release to Mining Weekly on Wednesday, October 21, Weir plc pointed out that Cameron would be bringing more than a quarter century of leadership experience, spanning mining operations, heavy equipment, technology-led solutions and global commercial roles.

value.title: De Beers makes first contribution to Botswana's Diamonds for Development Fund
value.snippet: Diamond miner De Beers Group has transferred its initial contribution of P1-billion to the Diamonds for Development Fund, in Botswana, marking a major milestone in the progress of the fund and its mandate to support the Southern African country's long-term economic diversification. The disbursement follows the establishment of the fund’s governance structures, including the appointment of Dr Akinwumi Adesina as the fund’s chairperson, as well as the appointment and onboarding of the ten-person independent board.

value.title: Westgold reaches stable two-million tonnes a year mine rate at Beta Hunt
value.snippet: ASX- and TSX-listed Westgold Resources has removed legacy mine infrastructure constraints to establish a platform that supports a sustained two-million-tonne-a-year mining rate at the Beta Hunt underground mine at Kambalda. Beta Hunt achieved a record annualised mining rate of two-million tonnes a year in September, before the interim primary ventilation system was commissioned (ahead of schedule at month-end).

value.title: First Quantum's expanded Zambia copper mine on track to exceed processing target
value.snippet: First Quantum Minerals' expanded Kansanshi copper mine in Zambia is on track to process about 27-million metric tons of ore in 2026, exceeding its design capacity by 8% and supporting a stronger production outlook, the company said on Wednesday. Kansanshi Mining's $1.2 billion S3 expansion project was commissioned in August 2025 and is expected to double the mine's copper output to about 277 000 metric tons annually.

value.title: Australia's Sarytogan Graphite publishes first DFS of two planned for Sarytogan project
value.snippet: ASX-listed Sarytogan Graphite finds in a definitive feasibility study (DFS) on the Upstream Sarytogan graphite project, in Kazakhstan, the potential to produce 50 000 t/y of graphite concentrate in varying sizes. The company plans to have 20 000 t/y classified into three sizes up 15 microns for drilling fluids, lubricants and friction products, 10 000 t/y of unclassified concentrate for the foundry and iron recarburiser market and 20 000 t/y for a planned downstream graphite business to make ultrahigh-purity fines and coated spherical purified graphite products.

value.title: Chile plans five new lithium tenders in push to double output
value.snippet: Chile plans to issue tenders for five more lithium projects next year as part of a drive to more than double output of the battery metal within a decade, Mining Minister Daniel Mas told Reuters. The world's second-biggest lithium producer wants the private sector to play a bigger role in developing new mines, Mas said in an interview during LME Week, an annual gathering of the global metals industry in London.

value.title: Namibia tin producer’s gross profit up fourfold on 80% revenue surge
value.snippet: Namibia tin producer Andrada Mining on Wednesday, October 21, reported a quadrupled-plus gross profit and an 80% revenue surge. Supporting this high performance in the six months ended August 31 was a 13% increase in tin production and an effective 57% tin price increase to $52 131/t.

value.title: Vulcan Elements partners with reseachers on quantum-mechanical rare earth innovation
value.snippet: American rare earth magnet manufacturer Vulcan Elements has partnered with research organisation North Carolina Collaboratory to advance development of high-performance rare earth magnets for defence and commercial technology applications. Particularly, research led by University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC-Chapel Hill) chemistry Professor Yosuke Kanai will help to develop a novel analytic capability using quantum-mechanical simulations to predict with significant accuracy how changes at the atomic level affect magnetic properties.

value.title: Sherritt granted US fuel licence as first step towards Moa Nickel restart
value.snippet: TSX-listed nickel and cobalt refiner Sherritt International Corporation has received a fuel licence from the US Department of Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) which authorises the purchase and delivery of fuel, fuel oil and sulphur to Sherritt's Moa Nickel mining and processing operations in Cuba. The operations have been under strain owing to US sanctions imposed on Cuba earlier this year, with Sherritt having ceased mining operations in Cuba and refinery operations in Canada. One particular challenge has been that of fuel supply disruption.

value.title: Rio Tinto, Rondo Energy assess large-scale heat battery integration at Yarwun refinery
value.snippet: US-headquartered Rondo Energy and global diversified miner Rio Tinto have started front-end engineering design (FEED) work on a 360 MWh energy storage project for deployment at the Yarwun alumina refinery near Gladstone, in Queensland. The Rondo heat battery project is supported by an initial $3.6-million grant from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) for the FEED stage, with another $38-million having been committed by ARENA for deployment.

value.title: Ghana moves to standardise mining pay amid local-content drive
value.snippet: Ghana has ordered its mining regulator to standardise pay and employment conditions across the industry, a move that could ease union concerns over a planned shift of mining operations from multinational companies to local contractors by December. Africa's top gold producer has directed miners to transfer operations to local contractors or face sanctions under local-content rules affecting major operators including Newmont, AngloGold Ashanti, Zijin and Ghana Manganese Company. Labour unions have opposed the policy, warning it could reduce workers' pay and benefits

value.title: At least $100bn of investment for 134 new lithium mines is needed for 2050 demand
value.snippet: To meet 2050 lithium demand, the equivalent of 134 new lithium mines will be needed, says supply chain researcher Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. This equates to a new mine every two months for the next 24 years, explains Benchmark Mineral Intelligence lithium product director Dr Cameron Perks.

value.title: Steel trader Luda Technology Group branches out to coal as first point of diversification
value.snippet: NYSE-listed industrial steel components trader Luda Technology Group has announced its entry into the Mongolia-China coal trading business. value.title: North America to drive growth in antimony market
value.snippet: With China's suspension of its ban on antimony exports to the US scheduled to expire on November 27, buyers and manufacturers face an important decision point for supply planning, sourcing strategies and price risk management, says research and consulting company Polaris Market Research. Polaris estimates the global antimony market was worth $1.12-billion in 2025 but is poised to reach $1.85-billion by 2034, marking a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.7%.

value.title: Gold Fields' South Deep aligning mining with education to strengthen job pathways
value.snippet: Gold Fields’ South Deep mine has signed memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with Sibanye-Stillwater, AngloGold Ashanti, Mienara, Phahama School of Specialisation and Westcol Technical and Vocational Education and Training College (WTVETC) to support a collaborative initiative aimed at addressing the growing gap between skills development and employment opportunities. The collaborative Siyakha Sonke initiative is South Deep mine's contribution to the Gold Fields group legacy programmes portfolio, a collection of long-term social investments designed to create sustainable opportunities and lasting benefits for host communities beyond the life of mining. Its programmes aim to strengthen community resilience, support sustainable development and promote long-term socioeconomic stability in host communities.

value.title: Hydrogen major Nel appoints Morten Holum CEO

value.title: African Critical Elements acquires Lepidico Canada, Namibian lithium asset

value.title: Uganda export earnings up 36% in August on higher gold receipts

value.title: Tesla now says it needs its own maps for FSD after years of dismissing maps
value.snippet: Tesla says it’s building its own maps to fix some of the most common problems with its “Full Self-Driving” system, including reading speed limits, parking, and choosing routes. The company’s head of AI described the effort on Tesla’s Q3 2026 earnings call. It’s a notable shift for a company whose CEO spent years arguing that self-driving systems relying on maps are brittle. And it shows Tesla’s fleet is now doing the same job Waymo’s cars do: mapping the roads so the self-driving system knows what it can’t reliably figure out on its own. Tesla fans argue that Waymo’s approach differs because it creates HD maps with lidar, but ultimately both are creating their own maps; if your argument is that Tesla’s maps are less well-defined and needed for driving for different reasons than Waymo’s, you don’t really have an argument. more…

value.title: Newmont beats quarterly profit estimates on higher gold prices, Cadia recovery

Gold prices averaged $4 204.59/oz during the quarter, up about 17.6% from a year earlier, as investors sought safe-haven assets despite a stronger dollar and inflation concerns tied to higher oil prices during the US war on Iran.

value.title: Nickel Industries says Indonesia cuts coming as Chinese producers weigh steep reductions

"There will be coordinated cuts across all of the operations within the IMIP," MD Justin Werner told analysts on an earnings call, without giving a percentage. "Certainly what we're seeing is the non-integrated producers ... are the ones that are going to suffer the hardest here."

value.title: Australia's Whitehaven Coal beats quarterly output estimates on Queensland strength
value.snippet: Australia's Whitehaven Coal beat market estimates for quarterly output on Friday, supported by robust production from its Queensland operations, and said it expected stronger cash generation through the remainder of the year. The coal miner reported managed run-of-mine (ROM) coal production of 11-million tons for the three-month period ended September 30, up from 9-million tons a year earlier and above the Visible Alpha consensus estimate of 9.5-million tons.

value.title: GM cancels deal with new US rare-earth magnet plant, documents say

The move spotlights the challenges Western firms face in building domestic rare-earths output and cutting their reliance on China, which produces about 90% of global permanent magnets.

value.title: Norsk Hydro flags higher smelting costs after quarterly profit miss

value.title: Iridium, ruthenium continue to outperform, Valterra Platinum reports
value.snippet: Minor platinum group metals (PGMs), particularly iridium and ruthenium, are continuing to outperform, supported by robust demand from emerging technology applications, Valterra Platinum reported on Friday, October 23. The price Valterra realised for iridium in the three months ended September 30 was $7 720/oz, compared with $4 287/oz in the corresponding period of last year. The price realised for ruthenium in the quarter was $1 583/oz, compared with $799/oz in the third quarter of last year.

value.title: European Metals' Geomet opts for cheaper, cleaner tech choice for Cinovec lithium processing
